question: 'Tulip Festival' is celebrated in which of the following city?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Srinagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Tulip Festival** is an annual event held in **Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir**, at the **Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden**, which is the largest tulip garden in Asia.

• The festival is celebrated during the blooming season of tulips, which typically occurs in the **spring months of March and April**.

• The garden spans an area of **about 30 hectares** and is home to over **1.5 million tulip bulbs**, featuring a variety of colors and species.

• The Tulip Festival aims to promote the **tourism industry in Kashmir** and showcases the region's stunning natural beauty, attracting both domestic and international tourists.

• It also includes **cultural events, local handicraft exhibitions, and traditional Kashmiri cuisine**, making it a comprehensive cultural experience for visitors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden:**

• Located in the foothills of the **Zabarwan Range** with a panoramic view of **Dal Lake**.

• Established in **2007** by the Government of Jammu & Kashmir to boost tourism and floriculture in the region.

• The garden features multiple terraces, each showcasing a wide variety of tulips and other flowers.

• **Importance of Tulip Festival:**

• It is one of the major attractions for tourists visiting Kashmir during spring.

• It contributes significantly to the region's economy by promoting local crafts, culture, and agriculture.

• The festival highlights the rich **biodiversity and horticulture** of Jammu & Kashmir.

• **Tourism in Kashmir:**

• Jammu & Kashmir is often referred to as **"Paradise on Earth"** due to its breathtaking natural beauty, including mountains, lakes, and gardens.

• Popular tourist attractions include **Dal Lake, Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Sonmarg, and Mughal Gardens**.

• The Tulip Festival adds a unique dimension to the region's tourism by focusing on horticultural and cultural diversity.

• **Other Tulip Festivals Around the World:**

• The **Keukenhof Tulip Festival** in the Netherlands is one of the most famous tulip festivals globally, featuring millions of tulips in bloom.

• The **Canadian Tulip Festival** in Ottawa celebrates the gift of tulips from the Netherlands as a symbol of international friendship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **History of the Tulip Garden:** The garden was initially known as the "Model Floriculture Center" and was later renamed after **Indira Gandhi**.

• **Types of Tulips:** The garden showcases a variety of tulips, including **single early tulips, double late tulips, fringed tulips, and parrot tulips**.

• **Accessibility:** The garden is located approximately **8 km from Srinagar city center** and is well-connected by road, making it easily accessible for tourists.

• **Economic Impact:** The festival has a significant impact on local businesses, including hotels, restaurants, and handicraft sellers, contributing to the overall development of the region.
